newsitem.title: UK: BA urges EU to block Air Liberte sale to AOM.
newsitem.headline: BA urges EU to block Air Liberte sale to AOM.

text.p: British Airways said it is urging the European Commission to block "with the utmost urgency" a bid by French regional airline AOM to buy its competitor Air Liberte, which went into receivership last week.
AOM is currently up for sale under a restructuring plan as a condition of state aid granted to its parent, the state-owned French bank Credit Lyonnais.

Allowing AOM to buy Air Liberte would be an illegal use of state aid, BA says in letters sent to European commissioners for transport and competition Neil Kinnock and Karel van Miert, because it would add to the liabilities facing the AOM Group, thereby contravening the conditions of the Credit Lyonnais aid.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation, the holding company charged with selling Credit Lyonnais assets under the state-supported rescue plan.

French newspaper Le Monde reported on Friday that the French government wants to create an airline by bringing together privately owned Eurolair and AOM and buying up the insolvent Air Liberte in order to keep out BA.
If BA were to buy Air Liberte it would stand to gain valuable slots at Paris' short haul Orly airport.

"French media have reported that the French authorities are seeking to arrange the sale of Air Liberte in such a way as to avoid its slots at Paris Orly being acquired by foreign airlines. New slots at Orly are no longer availabale because of restrictions imposed by the French authorities," said BA.
